title: Plantholt's overfull criterion for graphs of high minimum degree, with 1-factorization theorems for dense regular graphs (6/7 and 11/12)
abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of Theorem 1.2 of M. Plantholt, Overfull conjecture for graphs with high minimum degree (J. Graph Theory 47, 2004), and of a 1-factorization theorem for dense regular graphs in the style of Chetwynd and Hilton (1989). theorem_1_2: if c ≥ 3/4 is such that every regular graph of even order n and degree at least c n is 1-factorizable, and G has even order n with (3δ − Δ)/2 ≥ c n, then G is Class 1 (χ′ = Δ) if and only if G has no Δ-overfull subgraph. lineGraph_colorable_of_isRegular: a d-regular graph of even order 2n with 11 n ≤ 6 d is d-edge-colourable, i.e. 1-factorizable; this is a weaker form of Chetwynd–Hilton 1989, Theorem 2 (d ≥ ½(√7 − 1)|V|), proved with the same architecture. overfull_criterion: Plantholt's theorem with c = 11/12, i.e. if G has even order n and 11 n ≤ 6 (3δ − Δ), then G is Class 1 if and only if it has no Δ-overfull subgraph. lineGraph_colorable_of_isRegular67: the theorem of Chetwynd and Hilton (Proc. London Math. Soc. 50, 1985) that a d-regular graph of even order 2n with 12 n ≤ 7 d (degree at least 6/7 of the order) is 1-factorizable. overfull_criterion67: Plantholt's theorem with c = 6/7, i.e. even order n and 12 n ≤ 7 (3δ − Δ). Five statements. A Δ-overfull subgraph has an odd number ≥ 3 of vertices and more than Δ ⌊|V(H)|/2⌋ edges; edge colourings are colourings of the line graph.
